mainTopic: Reminding a forgetful witness, the משנה about dirt mounds that may hide a grave and how long people remember, and a new משנה on witnesses confirming their own signatures.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a discussion about witnesses who forgot their testimony. A צורבא מרבנן may be reminded even by the litigant himself, because he testifies only from his own real memory, as the story of רב אשי and רב כהנא shows. The גמרא then quotes a משנה in אהלות about dirt mounds that may hide a grave, where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about what counts as 'near' and 'old.' Reading 'city' and 'path' as any city or path would clash with ריש לקיש's rule that the חכמים leaned toward treating ארץ ישראל as טהור. רבי זירא answers that the משנה means a city or path next to a בית הקברות. רבי חנינא explains that women bury stillborn babies, and people with שחין bury fallen-off limbs, in mounds close to the city, so we still do not presume טומאה in ארץ ישראל. רב חסדא tries to learn from רבי מאיר that testimony is remembered for only sixty years. The גמרא rejects this, because a witness who is responsible for his testimony remembers far longer. A new משנה then asks when witnesses are believed to confirm their own signatures on a שטר, with רבי and the חכמים disagreeing, and the גמרא's analysis of רבי's view continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A Torah scholar may be reminded even by the litigant
steps.stepSummary: If the witness who forgot is a צורבא מרבנן, even the litigant himself may remind him of the testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the witness is a Torah scholar, even the litigant himself may remind him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier rule about reminding a witness who forgot his testimony. It adds that a צורבא מרבנן may be reminded even by the person the testimony is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we worry that a litigant who 'reminds' a witness is really feeding him a story. A צורבא מרבנן is trusted to testify only if he truly remembers on his own. So the worry falls away for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Even he himself, meaning the litigant

phrases.english: And if he is a Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the witness who forgot his testimony, from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: even [the litigant] himself [may remind him].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rules about reminding a witness from the previous part of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A צורבא מרבנן witness may be reminded even by the litigant, because he will testify only from his own real memory.

steps.title: רב אשי forgets, then remembers, testimony for רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא tried to remind רב אשי of a testimony. רב אשי at first did not remember, and later remembered and testified.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of רב אשי, who knew testimony for רב כהנא. רב כהנא asked him: Do you remember this testimony? He said: No. Wasn't it like this and this? He said: I don't know. In the end רב אשי remembered and testified for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show the rule about a תלמיד חכם being reminded by the litigant. The story continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא is the litigant himself, and he tries to remind רב אשי. רב אשי does not testify while he is unsure. He testifies only after he truly remembers.

phrases.english: Like that case of Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה יְדִיעַ לֵיהּ בְּסָהֲדוּתָא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא.
phrases.english: who knew testimony on behalf of Rav Kahana.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי דְּכִיר מָר הַאי סָהֲדוּתָא?
phrases.english: [Rav Kahana] said to him: Does the master remember this testimony?
He said to him: No.
[Rav Kahana asked:] Wasn't it like this and like this?
phrases.notes: Here רב כהנא, the litigant himself, is trying to jog רב אשי's memory.

phrases.english: He said to him: I don't know.
In the end, Rav Ashi remembered,
and he testified for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that shows the rule from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a תלמיד חכם reminded by the litigant still testifies only from his own memory.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב אשי and רב כהנא.

steps.title: רב אשי: I remembered on my own
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא was hesitant to rely on the testimony. רב אשי told him he had worked to remember it himself and was not relying on what רב כהנא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that רב כהנא was hesitant. He said to him: Do you think I am relying on you? I made an effort myself and I remembered.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב אשי explaining that his testimony came from his own memory. This is the point of the whole rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא worried that his own hints had shaped the testimony. רב אשי answers that a תלמיד חכם does not just repeat the litigant's version; he puts in the effort until he truly remembers. That is why the litigant may remind a צורבא מרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: I put effort on myself, I pushed myself

steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם may be reminded even by the litigant, because he testifies only after he truly remembers on his own, as רב אשי did.

phrases.english: He saw that Rav Kahana was hesitant.
He said to him: Do you think
that I am relying on you?
It is I who put effort on myself,
phrases.notes: Literally 'I threw upon my soul.' He means he worked hard to bring back the memory himself.

phrases.english: and I remembered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and spells out its point.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תלמיד חכם's testimony comes from his own memory, even if the litigant was the one who reminded him.

steps.title: The משנה about dirt mounds that may hide a grave
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in אהלות rules on when mounds of dirt are טמא because a body may be buried in them. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about what counts as 'near' and 'old.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Mounds near a city or a path, new or old, are טמא. Far mounds: new ones are טהור, old ones are טמא. What is near? Fifty אמות. What is old? Sixty years. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: near means there is no mound closer than it; old means no one remembers it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת about dirt mounds. It sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A near mound is always טמא, since a body may have been buried there. A far mound is טמא only if it is old: a new one is טהור, because people would still remember if someone had been buried in it. רבי מאיר gives fixed numbers, and רבי יהודה gives looser, common-sense measures.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: 'New' does not make every mound טהור. Only a far mound that is new is טהור; a near mound is טמא even if it is new.

phrases.english: We learned there [in a Mishnah]:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in אהלות 16:2.

phrases.english: Mounds of dirt that are near
either to a city or to a path,
whether new or old, are impure.
Those that are far:
the new ones are pure, the old ones are impure.
What counts as near? Fifty cubits.
And what counts as old? Sixty years.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Near means there is no [mound] nearer than it;
old means one that no person remembers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic. Like the witness rules, this משנה depends on how long people remember things.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Near mounds are טמא whether new or old. Far mounds are טהור if new and טמא if old. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about how to measure 'near' and 'old.'

steps.title: What do 'city' and 'path' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of city and path the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'city' and what is the 'path'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'city' and 'path.' This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the exact case the משנה describes. If we read these words too broadly, the ruling may clash with another rule.

phrases.english: What is a 'city' and what is a 'path'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which city and which path the משנה is talking about.

steps.title: Any city or path would clash with ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: If 'city' and 'path' mean any city or path, the משנה would be treating a mere doubt as טומאה. That goes against ריש לקיש, who said the חכמים looked for reasons to treat ארץ ישראל as טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'city' means a real city and 'path' means a real path, do we really assume טומאה from a doubt? But ריש לקיש said: They found a reason and declared ארץ ישראל טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple reading, any city or path, and attacks it using a rule of ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mound next to an ordinary city is only a doubtful grave. ריש לקיש teaches that the חכמים leaned toward treating ארץ ישראל as טהור whenever they could. So it is hard to say the משנה makes every such mound טמא.

phrases.english: If you say 'city' means an actual city,
and 'path' means an actual path,
do we assume impurity from a doubt?
But didn't Reish Lakish say:
They found a reason
and declared the Land of Israel pure.
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים, when unsure about an area, looked for a reason to treat it as טהור.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְּפֵיקָא מִי מַחְזְקִינַן טוּמְאָה? וְהָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries one answer to step 5's question and shows that it causes a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'city' and 'path' in the משנה as any city or path.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mound near an ordinary city is only a doubt, and ריש לקיש says doubts in ארץ ישראל were resolved toward טהרה.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a city or path next to the cemetery
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the משנה means a city next to a בית הקברות and the path to a בית הקברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: 'City' means a city next to the cemetery, and 'path' means the path to the cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The משנה is talking about places near a cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Near a cemetery, the chance that a body is buried in a mound is real, not just a far-off doubt. So ruling such mounds טמא does not go against ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
'City' means a city adjacent to the cemetery,
and 'path' means the path to the cemetery.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means any city or path, which would clash with ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means places near a cemetery, where a burial in a mound is a real possibility.

steps.title: The path makes sense, but why the city?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that people might bury a body in a mound along the cemetery path. But it asks why anyone would bury in a mound near the city, since everyone goes to the cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the path to the cemetery, because sometimes it happens at twilight, and they end up burying in a mound. But a city next to the cemetery: don't all of them go to the cemetery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges half of רבי זירא's answer. The path case is clear, but the city case still needs an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the path, people who run out of time might bury the body in a nearby mound. People in a city right next to a cemetery have no such pressure; they would just walk to the cemetery. So why should a mound near that city be טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the time between day and night

phrases.english: It makes sense for the path to the cemetery,
because sometimes it happens to be twilight,
phrases.notes: They could not reach the cemetery in time, for example before שבת began.

phrases.english: and it happens that they bury [the body] in a mound.
But a city adjacent to the cemetery,
don't they all go to the cemetery [to bury]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'city' half of רבי זירא's answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's explanation that 'city' means a city next to the cemetery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People near a cemetery bury there, so a mound near the city should not be suspected of hiding a grave.

steps.title: Why people bury in mounds near the city
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that women bury stillborn babies, and people with שחין bury their fallen-off arms, in mounds close to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Women bury their stillborn babies there, and people with boils bury their arms there. Up to fifty אמות from the city, a woman goes by herself. Farther than that, she takes someone with her, and then she just goes to the cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8: why would anyone bury something in a mound near the city instead of in the cemetery?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every burial gets a funeral trip to the cemetery. A woman quietly burying a stillborn baby, or a sick person burying a limb, will use a nearby mound. The woman goes alone only up to fifty אמות, which matches רבי מאיר's measure of 'near' in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a severe skin disease (boils) that can make limbs fall off
A cubit, a unit of length (about half a meter)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Because women bury their stillborn babies there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means in the mounds near the city, the ones the גמרא just asked about.

phrases.english: and people afflicted with boils bury their arms there.
Up to fifty cubits from the city
she goes by herself.
Farther than that, she takes a person with her,
and she goes to the cemetery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים קוֹבְרוֹת שָׁם נִפְלֵיהֶן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a real-life reason that explains the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone buries in the cemetery, so a mound near the city should not be suspect
steps.terutzMaskana: Small, private burials happen in nearby mounds up to fifty אמות from the city

steps.title: The general rule of no presumed impurity still stands
steps.stepSummary: Since anything farther than fifty אמות gets brought to the cemetery, we still do not assume טומאה in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, we do not presume טומאה in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up: the mounds are a special exception with a real reason, so ריש לקיש's general rule is not broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 worried that the משנה treats a plain doubt as טומאה. Now we see the mounds have a real basis for suspicion. Everywhere else, the general rule of treating ארץ ישראל as טהור stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: Mounds near a city or along the cemetery path are suspect only because people really do bury things there. This is an exception, and it does not change the rule that we do not presume טומאה in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Therefore,
we do not presume ritual impurity in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ, טוּמְאָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָא מַחְזְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי חנינא's answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש's rule holds; the mounds are a special case with a real reason behind them

steps.title: Learning a sixty-year memory limit from רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא suggests that רבי מאיר's sixty-year limit for an 'old' mound shows that a witness remembers testimony for up to sixty years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Learn from רבי מאיר that a person remembers testimony for up to sixty years, and does not remember it after that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא takes רבי מאיר's rule about mounds and tries to turn it into a general rule about how long witnesses remember things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said a mound counts as 'old' after sixty years, which suggests people no longer remember what happened there. רב חסדא wants to apply this to all testimony, which fits the larger סוגיא about how long witnesses can be trusted to remember.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, conclude from it

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Conclude from Rabbi Meir:
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי מאיר's rule in the משנה that a mound counts as 'old' after sixty years.

phrases.english: this testimony, up to sixty years,
is remembered;
more than that, it is not remembered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מֵרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new general rule from the משנה discussed earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony is remembered for sixty years and forgotten after that

steps.title: Rejecting the sixty-year rule for testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the mound case is different, because nobody was given responsibility for remembering it. A real witness who is responsible remembers much longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There, with the mound, nobody gave him the job of remembering. But here, since the testimony was his responsibility, he remembers even much longer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא and shows the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People forget about a mound because it was never their concern. A witness knows he may be called to testify, so he pays attention and remembers. That means the sixty-year limit cannot be applied to testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (a rejection)
It is placed on him, it is his responsibility

steps.whatToRemember: How long a person remembers depends on whether he was responsible for it. A witness who knows he may have to testify remembers even beyond sixty years.

phrases.english: But that is not so.
There, it is a case where it was not placed upon him.
phrases.notes: He means nobody gave this person the job of keeping track of the mound, so he didn't pay attention.

phrases.english: But here,
since it was placed upon him,
he remembers even much longer too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, הָתָם הוּא דְּלָא רַמְיָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The mound case has no responsibility to remember, but testimony does, so the two cannot be compared

steps.title: New משנה: each witness confirms both signatures
steps.stepSummary: If each of the two signing witnesses confirms his own signature and his friend's, they are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says, 'This is my handwriting and this is my friend's handwriting,' and the other says the same, they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about witnesses who signed a שטר and later come to בית דין to confirm the signatures are real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To confirm a שטר, each signature needs two witnesses to vouch for it. Here, each witness vouches for both signatures, so every signature has two people confirming it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
This one says: This is my handwriting,
and this is the handwriting of my fellow witness.
And that one says: This is my handwriting,
and this is the handwriting of my fellow witness —
these witnesses are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: כְּתַב יָדִי, וְזֶה כְּתַב יָדוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When each witness confirms both signatures, the שטר is confirmed

steps.title: רבי: each confirms only himself, so a third witness is needed
steps.stepSummary: If each witness confirms only his own signature, רבי says another witness must be added.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says, 'This is my handwriting,' and the other says, 'This is my handwriting,' they need to add another witness with them. This is רבי's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a harder case, where each witness vouches only for himself, and gives רבי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each signature has only one person confirming it, and that person is the signer himself. According to רבי, this is not enough, so a third person must join to confirm the signatures.

phrases.english: This one says: This is my handwriting,
and that one says: This is my handwriting —
they must add another witness with them,
this is the statement of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה אוֹמֵר: זֶה כְּתַב יָדִי, וְזֶה אוֹמֵר: זֶה כְּתַב יָדִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: when each witness confirms only his own signature, a third witness is required

steps.title: חכמים: a person is believed about his own signature
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say no extra witness is needed, because a person is believed to say 'this is my handwriting.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: They do not need to add another witness. A person is believed to say, 'This is my handwriting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view of the חכמים in the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that each witness confirming his own signature is enough. Together, the two witnesses confirm the whole שטר.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that witnesses who each confirm both signatures are believed. They argue only when each witness confirms just his own: רבי requires a third witness, and the חכמים do not.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
They do not need to add another witness with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נֶאֱמָן אָדָם לוֹמַר זֶה כְּתַב יָדִי.
phrases.english: rather, a person is believed to say: This is my handwriting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינָם צְרִיכִין לְצָרֵף עִמָּהֶן אַחֵר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: each witness confirming his own signature is enough

steps.title: The גמרא begins analyzing רבי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by starting to explain רבי's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you come to analyze this, say that according to רבי...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to explain the reasoning behind רבי's opinion, and the sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase כשתימצי לומר signals that the גמרא is about to lay out how to understand each side. Here it begins with רבי, and the actual explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: When you come to analyze it, you will find that

phrases.english: GEMARA:
When you analyze it, say:
according to the statement of Rabbi
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה
